more_info.overview: Sorbitan monolaurate is a mixture of partial esters of sorbitol and its anhydrides with lauric acid; the commercial preparation is not a single pure ester. Its emulsifying role is to help form or maintain mixtures of oil and water in the finished food. Made from partial esters of sorbitol and its anhydrides with lauric acid. The specification does not identify a single biological source for the fatty acid. The preparation can be an amber viscous liquid, pale beads or flakes, or a firm waxy solid.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; other; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products; sweet baked goods.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
more_info.origin: Made from partial esters of sorbitol and its anhydrides with lauric acid. The specification does not identify a single biological source for the fatty acid.
more_info.dietary_restrictions: The fatty-acid feedstock is not specified as exclusively plant derived. Vegan, vegetarian, halal and kosher suitability cannot be established without the supplier identifying the raw material and processing.
more_info.daily_intake: 10 mg sorbitan/kg body weight/day, combined sorbitan esters (EFSA, 2017).
more_info.side_effects:
Assessed food-use exposure stayed below the group limit.
Animal toxicity evidence informed its safety margin.
